explanation.title: Spanish Imperative Mood: Giving Commands & Instructions

sections.subtitle: Informal Affirmative Commands (Tú)
sections.content: For tú, use the 3rd person singular (él/ella) present indicative form. Regular: habla (speak), come (eat), escribe (write). Common irregulars: decir→di, hacer→haz, ir→ve, poner→pon, salir→sal, ser→sé, tener→ten, venir→ven. Examples: '¡Habla más despacio!' (Speak more slowly!), '¡Come la comida!' (Eat the food!), '¡Haz tu tarea!' (Do your homework!). This is the most common command form in everyday Spanish.

sections.subtitle: Informal Negative Commands (Tú)
sections.content: For negative tú commands, use 'no' + present subjunctive (tú form). Regular: no hables (don't speak), no comas (don't eat), no escribas (don't write). Irregulars follow subjunctive: no seas (don't be), no vayas (don't go), no hagas (don't do), no digas (don't say), no tengas (don't have). Examples: '¡No hables!' (Don't speak!), '¡No comas eso!' (Don't eat that!), '¡No vayas!' (Don't go!). Remember: negative commands ALWAYS use subjunctive for all persons.

sections.subtitle: Formal Commands (Usted/Ustedes)
sections.content: For usted and ustedes, ALWAYS use present subjunctive forms (affirmative AND negative). Usted: hable (speak), coma (eat), escriba (write), sea (be), vaya (go), haga (do). Ustedes: hablen, coman, escriban, sean, vayan, hagan. Negative: add 'no' before: no hable, no hablen. Examples: '¡Hable más despacio!' (Speak more slowly! - formal), '¡No hablen aquí!' (Don't speak here! - formal plural). Ustedes is used for plural 'you' in Latin America (formal AND informal) and formal plural in Spain.

sections.subtitle: Vosotros Commands (Spain)
sections.content: AFFIRMATIVE: Replace final 'r' of infinitive with 'd': hablar→hablad, comer→comed, vivir→vivid. No irregulars in affirmative! Examples: '¡Hablad!' (Speak! - you all), '¡Comed!' (Eat! - you all). NEGATIVE: Use present subjunctive (vosotros form): no habléis, no comáis, no viváis, no seáis, no vayáis. Examples: '¡No habléis!' (Don't speak! - you all). Note: Vosotros is primarily used in Spain; Latin America uses ustedes for plural you.

sections.subtitle: Pronoun Placement with Commands
sections.content: AFFIRMATIVE commands: Attach pronouns to the END of the verb (one word): '¡Hazlo!' (Do it!), '¡Dámelo!' (Give it to me!), '¡Siéntate!' (Sit down!), '¡Levántate!' (Get up!). Add accent marks to maintain original stress. NEGATIVE commands: Pronouns go BEFORE the verb (separate): '¡No lo hagas!' (Don't do it!), '¡No me lo des!' (Don't give it to me!), '¡No te sientes!' (Don't sit down!). Order with two pronouns: indirect before direct (me lo, te la, se los). Reflexive pronoun 'te' attaches: siéntate, levántate.

sections.subtitle: Nosotros Commands (Let's...)
sections.content: Use present subjunctive (nosotros form) for 'let's' commands. Affirmative: hablemos (let's speak), comamos (let's eat), vayamos (let's go), seamos (let's be). Alternative for 'ir': use 'vamos' (not vayamos) for affirmative: '¡Vamos!' (Let's go!). Negative: no hablemos, no comamos, no vayamos (use subjunctive), no seamos. With pronouns: affirmative attaches them (drop final 's' before 'nos'): sentémonos (let's sit down - not sentemosnos), levantémonos (let's get up). Negative: pronouns go before: no nos sentemos.

questions.question: How do you form affirmative tú commands for regular verbs?

answers.text: Use 3rd person singular present indicative (él/ella form)
Use 2nd person singular present indicative (tú form)

questions.hint: Same as 'he/she' present form: habla (he speaks) → ¡Habla! (speak!).

questions.question: What is the affirmative tú command of 'hablar'?
questions.hint: Use the él/ella form: él habla → ¡Habla!

questions.question: What is the affirmative tú command of 'comer'?
questions.hint: Use the él/ella form: él come → ¡Come!

questions.question: What is the irregular affirmative tú command of 'hacer'?
questions.hint: This is one of 8 common irregular tú commands. Think 'haz-lo' (do it).

questions.question: What is the irregular affirmative tú command of 'ir'?
questions.hint: Irregular and very short. Same as 'ver' command: ¡Ve!

questions.question: Which verbs have irregular affirmative tú commands?

answers.text: decir, hacer, ir, poner, salir, ser, tener, venir

questions.hint: 8 common verbs: di, haz, ve, pon, sal, sé, ten, ven. Memorize these!

questions.question: How do you form negative tú commands?
questions.hint: Negative commands ALWAYS use subjunctive forms.

questions.question: What is the negative tú command of 'hablar'?
questions.hint: Use subjunctive: no + hables (present subjunctive tú form).

questions.question: What is the negative tú command of 'ir'?
questions.hint: Negative uses subjunctive. Ir subjunctive: vaya, vayas, vaya...

questions.question: How do you form usted/ustedes commands (both affirmative and negative)?
questions.hint: Formal commands ALWAYS use subjunctive (unlike tú affirmative commands).

questions.question: What is the usted command of 'hablar' (affirmative)?
questions.hint: Usted commands use subjunctive: hable (formal singular 'speak').

questions.question: What is the ustedes command of 'comer' (affirmative)?
questions.hint: Ustedes commands use subjunctive: coman (formal/Latin America plural 'eat').

questions.question: How do you form affirmative vosotros commands?
questions.hint: hablar → hablad, comer → comed, vivir → vivid. No irregulars!

questions.question: What is the affirmative vosotros command of 'hablar'?
questions.hint: Replace -r with -d: hablar → hablad (speak, you all - Spain).

questions.question: How do you form negative vosotros commands?

answers.text: no + infinitive minus r plus d

questions.hint: Negative commands use subjunctive: no habléis, no comáis.

questions.question: Where do pronouns go with affirmative commands?

answers.text: Attached to the end of the verb

questions.hint: Forms one word: hazlo (do it), dámelo (give it to me).

questions.question: '¡Hazlo!' means 'Do it!' - Why the accent on 'Haz'?

answers.text: No accent on 'Hazlo' - accent maintains stress when pronoun attaches
Lo always requires accent before it

questions.hint: Actually: ¡Hazlo! (no accent). Add accent when needed to maintain original stress.

questions.question: Where do pronouns go with negative commands?
questions.hint: No lo hagas (Don't do it), No te sientes (Don't sit down).

questions.question: '¡Siéntate!' means...
questions.hint: Affirmative tú command of sentarse: sienta + te = siéntate (accent added).

questions.question: How do you form nosotros commands (let's...)?
questions.hint: Hablemos (let's speak), Comamos (let's eat) - uses subjunctive.

questions.question: What is the affirmative nosotros command of 'ir' (let's go)?
questions.hint: Exception! Use vamos for affirmative 'let's go', not vayamos.

questions.question: '¡No nos sentemos!' means...

answers.text: Let's not sit down! (pronouns before negative command)

questions.hint: Negative nosotros command: no + pronoun + subjunctive.

questions.question: 'Sentémonos' (let's sit down) - Why drop the 's'?

answers.text: Drop final 's' before reflexive 'nos' in affirmative

questions.hint: Sentemos + nos: drop the 's' → sentémonos (phonetic rule).
